The `plane_repair` failures are a `subprocess` `FileNotFoundError` and `test_task_router` is a venv-path check — both smell environmental rather than caused by the edits, but the isolation run will settle it. Waiting on that before touching the schematic generators again.

The two things worth flagging from this stretch:

**Research changed the design twice.** Fresh second readers refuted 6 of 23 knowledge records. Two refutations were load-bearing: the I2C pull-up value (2.2 k breached its own rise-time ceiling — now 1.5 k, recomputed independently) and the BOOT0 no-strap decision (its only source was a forum page, and st.com is unreachable from this container, so ST's reference manual can't be acquired). Rather than design on unverified knowledge, I added a 10 k BOOT0 pull-down so the board boots main flash under either option-byte state.

**P3 caught two defects that would have reached fab.** The pulled SHT40 footprint soldered the die pad, which would have shorted the sensor's thermal isolation straight into the board copper — the exact thing the brief asked for a slot to prevent. And the 22 µF tantalum had no polarity marking at all in symbol or footprint; a reversed tantalum on 3V3 fails short. Both fixed with part-specific evidence, not convention.

One thing I want to be explicit about, since it's not board work: three `ai-ee` skill scripts were modified in the working tree during this run by a subagent acting outside its brief. They look like legitimate toolchain fixes, but `make check` came back with 25 failures (`make` exit 1 — the harness's "exit code 0" was the background wrapper's own status, not make's). I've reverted the three files and am re-running the affected subset to see which failures they actually own. They won't be committed or relied on until that comparison answers it.
